What is Tribes?

  • The Tribes franchise is a series of first-person shooters for the PC originally released in 1998 with Starsiege: Tribes, and was developed by Dynamix. A sequel, Tribes 2, was released in 2001 also by Dynamix/GarageGames. In 2004 Tribes: Vengeance was released by Irrational Games, and in 2012 Hi-Rez Studios released Tribes: Ascend. A console version of Tribes 2 came out in 2002 for the PlayStation 2 called Tribes Aerial Assault.

Where can I download Tribes?

  • Download Tribes: Ascend
  • Download Tribes: Vengeance
  • Download Tribes 2
  • Download Starsiege: Tribes

Every Tribes game is free to download and play?!

  • Yep. Starsiege: Tribes and Tribes 2 were released as freeware to promote the launch of Tribes: Vengeance in 2004. Tribes: Vengeance has been free to download for years, unofficially at least. Tribes: Ascend is a F2P game, meaning it's completely free to download and play.

What about Tribes: Aerial Assault?

  • We don't speak of that game.

What is the current playerbase of Tribes like?

  • Starsiege: Tribes, Tribes 2, and Tribes: Vengeance all have very low playerbases these days. Tribes: Ascend is the most populated of all Tribes games. You can view current player traffic and match stats for Tribes: Ascend here. As of writing, Ascend has roughly 750-1000 unique players per hour and 4000 per day. The current status of the previous Tribes games can be viewed in the Tribes General section in the sidebar.

What is the current development status of Tribes?

  • None of the Tribes games receive developer support anymore. Starsiege: Tribes and Tribes 2 saw decent support from their developers post-release, though support for Tribes: Vengeance was essentially non-existent after release and was deemed and overall commercial failure. Hi-Rez Studios launched Tribes: Ascend in April of 2012 and ended development in March of 2013, however they still provide servers to play on. While the previous Tribes games still get updates from the remaining dedicated community, community updates for Tribes: Ascend are much harder and essentially non-existent due to the restrictions put in place by Hi-Rez Studios and the overall complexities of Unreal Engine 3. However, that hasn't stopped the community from providing their own custom configurations to help improve game performance and other tweaks, some of which can be found in the sidebar under Player Guides and Gameplay Tweaks.

What is Magic Chain? Will it get me banned? Where can I get it?

As ChoiSeung-hyun puts it:

Makes projectiles more 1:1, meaning they're really where you see them. This feels like a mixture of simulated projectiles on with simulated projectiles off. It's hard to describe but very helpful and makes chaining much easier in sub optimal pings. This is essentially what Simulated Projectiles off should have been, but Hi-Rez messed it up.

Lowers Rate of Fire on weapons that are tied to ping such as, throwing knives, nova colt, swag blaster, etc. It is not perfect and can't compensate at high pings, so don't expect 0ping knives ROF at 200ping. It works very well with knives and the swag blaster but only shaves off a bit of the ROF of nova colt. The throwing knives animation will be bugged, this is a tradeoff you'll have to deal with sorry..

As for getting banned, make sure you run the program as administrator (right-click, Run as administrator). If you don't then you will be banned.

You can get a copy of Magic Chain here, which includes Winject (i.e. acdontop.exe) and MagicChain v3 in both Red and Green versions, plus MagicChain v4 in Red version. If your anti-virus flags ACDontop.exe is a trojan this is normal and nothing to worry about. More information about Magic Chain can be found in this thread.

What are these 'pubs' and 'pugs' I keep hearing about?

  • Public matches are commonly referred to as 'pubs', which are matches you play by simply firing up the game and joining a random server. 'Pugs' is short for Pick-up Games, which are:

PUG is an acronym for 'Pick Up Game'. It's a casual but organized game of 'capture the flag' in Tribes: Ascend consisting of 2 teams of 7-9 players.

Each team is picked by a captain who picks players based on their preferred role (such as flag capper, flag defense etc).

The teams then play each other on a private server, making heavy use of voice communication to coordinate the offense and enforce the defense.

This coordination leads to intense, fast-paced and clutch play, which leads to some ridiculously fun times.

More information about PUGs can be found here.
